name: Inebu One
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Crowther, Melissa. 2001. All the One language(s): comparing linguistic and ethnographic definitions of language in New Guinea. Honours thesis (252pp).

sources.citation: Baker, Brett, Mark Donohue & Janet Fletcher. 2020/2021. Australia and New Guinea. Ch. 26 in C. Gussenhoven & A. Chen (eds), The Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody, 383-395. Oxford: OUP. Author accepted manuscript, Minerva Access hdl 11343/275209.
sources.note: sec. 26.4.1 (AAM p. 8; published p. 391): 'One [Torricelli; Sandaun, PNG] regularly assigns stress to the penultimate syllable, but verbs allow for stress on either syllable of the final foot, resulting in contrasts such as [ˈte.re] chop and [te.ˈre] howl... *[te.ˈli] with final stress is not a possible noun.' Generic 'One' = Donohue's field variety, Molmo One (Donohue 2000 fn.1); not attributed to Inebu One.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2007. Lexicography for your friends. In J. Siegel, J. Lynch & D. Eades (eds), Language Description, History and Development: Linguistic indulgence in memory of Terry Crowley (CLL 30), 395-405. Amsterdam: Benjamins. doi:10.1075/cll.30.37don
sources.note: Author's copy via Wayback (papuan.linguistics.anu.edu.au). About the Molmo One community dictionary (Sikale, Crowther & Donohue 2001); no occurrence of stress, accent, tone, syllable or Inebu in the text layer.
Phonology section gives Molmo One segments (from Foley 2018) only; Inebu One appears only as a ward location; cites Crowther 2001 for dialectology. No stress.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog for oin (as of 2025-11-04) and Ethnologue (c. 2016) entry 'One, Inebu'.
sources.note: OLAC lists only a transnewguinea.org wordlist, Glottolog, PARADISEC Laycock notebook DL2-006, Ethnologue and LinguistList -- no grammar or phonology. Ethnologue: 1,300 speakers (2000 M. Crowther), villages Alkula, Inebu, Kalema, Windiple, 'Dialects: None known'; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark & Melissa Crowther. 2005. Meeting in the middle: interaction in North-Central New Guinea. In A. Pawley, R. Attenborough, J. Golson & R. Hide (eds), Papuan Pasts (Pacific Linguistics 572), 167-184. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: The only source with Inebu One data: pp.178-179 twelve Inebu lexemes in a Romei/Inebu/Siama comparison; p.180 Table 2 Inebu consonants p t m n f s w l y; p.181 Table 3 vowels i e ɛ a o u; p.181: 'Tonal systems are consistently absent in the Torricelli languages (relevant here are the One varieties)'; p.182 Table 4 'Comparative suprasegmental inventories': Inebu row empty (no pitch contrasts). Nothing at all on stress placement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record for Inebu One [ineb1235] and reference record 77430 (Crowther 2001).
sources.note: No descriptive reference; 'most extensive descriptions' = Crowther 2001 and Laycock 1968, both classed wordlist_or_less. Crowther 2001 (hhtype overview;comparative;wordlist, v+247 pp.) covers the villages In = Inebu and Bi = Biako for Inebu One [oin].

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 767-780. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Family-level phonology paragraph (p. 769) illustrated from Olo; nothing on stress; One only in the classification list.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra.
sources.note: Entry 12 ONE (Aunalei, Onele, Oni): villages incl. Inebu, Piako, Alkula; 'Test DCL67 (Simbi, Auke/Inebu)... see Laycock (1968:1)' -- i.e. Laycock's 1967 One test wordlist was taken from an Inebu speaker. No phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In B. Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
